title: Exceptional restriction of a Verdier dual
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of schemes
[def-weil-closed-immersion], with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$.
Choose the small etale sites or the small pro-etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; in the pro-etale case
assume that $j$ is quasi-compact, meaning that the inverse image of each
quasi-compact open is quasi-compact. Let $\Lambda_T$ be a sheaf of commutative
rings on the chosen site of $T$, and use $\Lambda_Z=i^{-1}\Lambda_T$ and
$\Lambda_U=j^{-1}\Lambda_T$ as coefficient sheaves. Write
$\mathcal D(W)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_W))$ for the ordinary unbounded
derived category of module sheaves
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].
Use the exact inverse images $i^*=i^{-1}$, $j^*=j^{-1}$ and the closed direct
image $Ri_*=i_*$, applied termwise to complexes. Suppose that $i_*$ has a
right adjoint $Ri^!:\mathcal D(T)\to\mathcal D(Z)$, that is, natural bijections
$\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*N,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N,Ri^!L)$
for all $N\in\mathcal D(Z)$ and $L\in\mathcal D(T)$.

For any $\omega_T\in\mathcal D(T)$ fix
$\omega_Z=Ri^!\omega_T$, and put
$D_TK=R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_T}(K,\omega_T)$ and
$D_ZM=R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_Z}(M,\omega_Z)$, using the derived internal Hom
[def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then for every $K\in\mathcal D(T)$ there is
a natural isomorphism
$$
\alpha_K:Ri^!D_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_Zi^*K.
$$
This assertion does not use biduality or require boundedness,
constructibility, or finite Tor amplitude of $K$ or $\omega_T$.

proof.text: The tensor-Hom and exceptional-adjunction calculation constructs one common left adjoint for the two displayed functors on the small etale site. This is recorded by the intermediate common-left-adjunction theorem in the Lean module; its proof follows the six blueprint steps (closed-support projection, tensor-Hom currying, and the two exceptional adjunctions).
Two right adjoints of a common left adjoint are naturally isomorphic by uniqueness of right adjoints. Applying the generic categorical bridge gives the required natural isomorphism.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion and suppose the
ambient exceptional adjoints are defined, with
$\omega_Z=Ri^!\omega_T$. Put
$D_T=R\mathcal Hom_T(-,\omega_T)$ and
$D_Z=R\mathcal Hom_Z(-,\omega_Z)$. Then there is a natural
isomorphism

$$
\alpha_K:Ri^!D_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_Zi^*K.
$$

proof.text:
For any test complex $N$ on $Z$, the tensor adjunction of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the closed exceptional
adjunction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N,Ri^!D_TK)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*N\otimes^L K,\omega_T)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*(N\otimes^L i^*K),\omega_T)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N\otimes^L i^*K,\omega_Z)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N,D_Zi^*K).
\end{aligned}
$$

The middle projection identity holds for a closed immersion in the
recollement of [def-weil-open-closed-recollement] because
$i_*$ is exact and fully faithful, and its stalkwise extension by
zero commutes with tensor product; flat resolutions give the derived
identity. The calculation localizes on every etale test object, so it
identifies the internal Hom objects. Yoneda proves the isomorphism.
Every arrow is defined by adjunction and evaluation, giving naturality.
